chapter.heading: The Priestly Ministry Begins
chapter.v:
It came
to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel. [Ezek. 43:27]

And he
said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a young bull as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering, without blemish, and offer them before the Lord. [Ex. 29:21; Lev.]

And to
the children of Israel you shall speak, saying, ‘Take a kid of the goats as a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both of the first year, without blemish, as a burnt offering, [Lev. 4:23, 28; Ezra 6:17; 10:19]

also a
bull and a ram as peace offerings, to sacrifice before the Lord, and a grain offering mixed with oil; for today the Lord will appear to you.’ ” [Lev. 2:4 e Ex. 29:43; Lev. 9:6,]

So they
brought what Moses commanded before the tabernacle of meeting. And all the congregation drew near and stood before the Lord.

Then Moses
said, “This is the thing which the Lord commanded you to do, and the glory of the Lord will appear to you.”

And Moses
said to Aaron, “Go to the altar, offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Offer the offering of the people, and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded.” [Lev. 4:3;]

Aaron therefore
went to the altar and killed the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself.

Then the
sons of Aaron brought the blood to him. And he dipped his finger in the blood, put it on the horns of the altar, and poured the blood at the base of the altar.

But the
fat, the kidneys, and the fatty lobe from the liver of the sin offering he burned on the altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses. [Ex. 23:18; Lev. 8:16]

The flesh
and the hide he burned with fire outside the camp. [Lev. 4:11,]

And he
killed the burnt offering; and Aaron’s sons presented to him the blood, which he sprinkled all around on the altar. [Lev. 1:5; 8:19]

Then they
presented the burnt offering to him, with its pieces and head, and he burned them on the altar. [Lev. 8:20]

And he
washed the entrails and the legs, and burned them with the burnt offering on the altar. [Lev. 8:21]

Then he
brought the people’s offering, and took the goat, which was the sin offering for the people, and killed it and offered it for sin, like the first one. [[Is. 53:10; Heb. 2:17; 5:3]]

And he
brought the burnt offering and offered it according to the prescribed manner. [Lev. 1:1-13]

Then he
brought the grain offering, took a handful of it, and burned it on the altar, besides the burnt sacrifice of the morning. [Ex. 29:38,]

He also
killed the bull and the ram as sacrifices of peace offerings, which were for the people. And Aaron’s sons presented to him the blood, which he sprinkled all around on the altar, [Lev. 3:1-11]

and the
fat from the bull and the ram—the fatty tail, what covers the entrails and the kidneys, and the fatty lobe attached to the liver;

but the
breasts and the right thigh Aaron waved as a wave offering before the Lord, as Moses had commanded. [Ex. 29:24, 26, 27; Lev. 7:30-34]

Then Aaron
lifted his hand toward the people, blessed them, and came down from offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and peace offerings.

And Moses
and Aaron went into the tabernacle of meeting, and came out and blessed the people. Then the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people,

and fire
came out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces. [Gen. 4:4; Judg. 6:21; 2 Chr. 7:1; Ps. 20:3 u Ezra 3:11 v 1 Kin. 18:38,]
